questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Many Kingdoms after the Guptas' refers to.
questions.a: From the sixth to the tenth centuries no single power ruled the subcontinent: kingdoms rose and fell across the north, and the south saw the Pallavas, Pandyas, Chalukyas and, later, the Cholas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Many Kingdoms after the Guptas'.
questions.a: Political division did not stop the flow of trade, temples and texts across the regions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Many Kingdoms after the Guptas' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Kingdoms of the South and the North

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Kingdoms of the South and the North' refers to.
questions.a: In the Deccan and the south, the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas, Pallavas and Pandyas built temple cities and fleets, while in the north kingdoms such as those of Harsha and later the Gurjara-Pratiharas held sway.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Kingdoms of the South and the North'.
questions.a: Region by region, local powers matured: each left its own style of temples, inscriptions and administration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Kingdoms of the South and the North' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'The Tripartite Struggle' refers to.
questions.a: For over two centuries the Palas, the Gurjara-Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas fought a tripartite struggle for Kanauj, the prized city on the Ganga; the long war drained all three without a lasting victor.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Tripartite Struggle'.
questions.a: Kanauj's prestige outvalued its fields: the contest shows how symbol and status drove medieval war.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'The Tripartite Struggle', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: struggle = palas + pratiharas + rashtrakutas over kanauj

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Learning, Mathematics and Culture' refers to.
questions.a: The age kept learning alive: mathematics and astronomy advanced, Sanskrit kavyas were composed, and temple architecture, from Nagara towers to Dravida vimanas, rose across the land.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Learning, Mathematics and Culture'.
questions.a: Culture outlives dynasties: the maths, poems and temples of this age outlasted every throne that ordered them.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Learning, Mathematics and Culture' taught, and from which source text?
